title: Check out new costs for military families as Tricare open season starts
description:
Military families can compare their options through Tricare Prime and Tricare Select, with the help of cost information released by Tricare officials last week.
Active-duty families, whether in Tricare Prime or Tricare Select, don’t pay enrollment fees.
Open season applies to those enrolled in or eligible for Tricare Prime or Tricare Select.
Open season doesn’t apply to individual active-duty service members, or to Tricare for Life, or to the premium -based plans of Tricare Reserve Select, Tricare Retired Reserve and Tricare Young Adult.
Active-duty family members, retirees and their eligible family members and Selected Reserve members and their families are eligible for FEDVIP vision coverage.
text:
With Tricare open season underway and news of cost increases in the 4% range, military families should review their healthcare costs in the military system and their needs for 2027.

This year’s Tricare open season started Monday and ends Dec.8. Military families can compare their options through Tricare Prime and Tricare Select, with the help of cost information released by Tricare officials last week.

Generally, those who have been paying out-of-pocket for healthcare under Tricare in 2026 will pay extra in 2027, according to the new fee schedules. Overall, for these groups, the co-payment increases are about 4%, or $1 to $3 for outpatient visits. Increases of another 4% apply to enrollment fees for retirees and their families who aren’t yet Medicare-eligible. The largest enrollment fee is for certain retirees in Tricare Select, who will pay $1,233 to enroll their family in 2027, up from $1,191 in 2026.

Active-duty families, whether in Tricare Prime or Tricare Select, don’t pay enrollment fees.

Open season applies to those enrolled in or eligible for Tricare Prime or Tricare Select. Beneficiaries can make changes to their health coverage, such as switching from Tricare Prime to Tricare Select, or moving from individual to family enrollment. Depending on the plan, Tricare costs may include enrollment fees, premiums, cost-shares and co-payments.

It’s also the 2026 Federal Benefits Open Season, beginning Monday and ending Dec. 14.

Some Tricare beneficiaries are eligible for the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program, or FEDVIP. In addition, active-duty service members can enroll in and make their annual selections for the dependent care flexible spending program and healthcare flexible spending program — two tax-saving programs that can help defray some of the costs of childcare and healthcare. This is the Federal Flexible Spending Account Program, or FSAFEDS.

Both FSAFEDS and FEDVIP are administered by BENEFEDS for the Office of Personnel Management.

Any changes made to Tricare plans, FEDVIP or FSAFEDS will take effect Jan. 1, 2027. If you’re eligible for these plans, now is the time to enroll; otherwise, you’ll have to wait until a qualifying life event, such as the birth or adoption of a child, marriage, divorce, moving or changes to other health insurance.

Those who are satisfied with their current Tricare or FEDVIP plan don’t need to take action.

Open season doesn’t apply to individual active-duty service members, or to Tricare for Life, or to the premium -based plans of Tricare Reserve Select, Tricare Retired Reserve and Tricare Young Adult. These premium-based plans can be purchased at any time during the year, but those in Tricare Young Adult with either the Prime or Select options can change plans only during open enrollment or a qualifying life event.

Visit Tricare.mil/openseason to find information about making changes online, by phone or by mailing an enrollment form to the regional contractor.

The plans

Tricare Prime is a health maintenance organization-style plan in which you get most of your care from a primary care manager, with referrals required for specialty care. There is no deductible.

Active-duty service members, their family members and transitional survivors don’t pay enrollment fees or out-of-pocket costs for covered services in Prime, unless they get non-emergency care without a referral, use non-network providers without authorization or use a pharmacy other than a military pharmacy.

Retirees, their families and all others pay enrollment fees and out-of-pocket costs for covered services except for preventive care.

Meanwhile, Tricare Select is a preferred provider organization-style plan in which you choose your Tricare-authorized provider and aren’t required to get referrals for most services. There are deductibles, co-payments and cost shares.

The costs

By law, there are differences in some costs based on when the sponsor entered the military. Those who entered before Jan. 1, 2018, are part of Group A, while those who enter on or after Jan. 1, 2018, are part of Group B.

Active-duty service members don’t have out-of-pocket costs for Tricare, but their family members may, depending on their health plan, the sponsor’s pay grade and group, the type of care and where they get their care.

There aren’t co-payments for any group for preventive care visits. For other covered services, such as primary care visits and specialty care outpatient visits, some co-pays will increase by $1 to $3 per visit, with some outliers.

For example, for some of those in Tricare Select, emergency room visit costs will go up by $4 or $5. For active-duty family members in Group A using Tricare Select, the cost per emergency room visit increases by $4, from $103 in 2026 to $107 in 2027.

Active-duty members, family members and transitional survivors don’t pay annual enrollment fees. But for retirees and their family members, the fees increase by about 4% in 2027. They’ll range from $396 for an individual Group A retiree in Prime to $1,233.96 for a Group B retiree plus their family in Tricare Select.

For active-duty family members in Tricare Prime, there’s no annual deductible, which is the out-of-pocket cost required before Tricare kicks in.

Those in Tricare Select have annual deductibles, which have increased by about 4% for those in Group B, who entered the military after Jan. 1, 2018. For example, for a family whose service member is E4 and below, the annual deductible increases by $5, to $137. Families of those in the ranks of E5 and above will see their deductible increased by $14, to $411.

Pharmacy costs won’t change in 2027. Beneficiaries can get most prescriptions filled at military pharmacies at no cost, and they can also get prescriptions through the Tricare Pharmacy Home Delivery program and at retail pharmacies in the Tricare network.

The largest cost increases, announced earlier, are in the premium-based plans. Those include:

Tricare Young Adult Prime, for members’ unmarried adult dependents ages 21 to 26: Costs increase by 12.5 % to $893 per month in 2027, compared to $794 in 2026.

Tricare Young Adult Select: Costs increase by 8.5% to $394 per month in 2027 from $363 in 2026.

Tricare Reserve Select, for qualified Selected Reserve and their family members: Costs increase by 4.5% for service members only to $60.54 per month in 2027 from $57.88 in 2026. Adding family, the cost is $307.48, up 7.2% per month from $286.66 in 2026.

Tricare Retired Reserve: $707.59 per month for service members only, up 9.5% from $645.90 in 2026. Adding family, costs total $1,697.70, up 9.6% from $1,548.30 in 2026.

Dental and vision

Families of active duty, National Guard and Reserve service members, as well as Guardsmen and reservists who aren’t on active duty, are eligible for the Tricare Dental Program. That program requires a separate enrollment. The premiums will stay the same through Feb. 28, 2027.

Most retirees and their family members are eligible for dental coverage under the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program, or FEDVIP. Visit benefeds.gov to compare choices of dental plans available by ZIP code and to enroll or make changes to an existing plan. FEDVIP open season ends Dec. 14.

Active-duty family members, retirees and their eligible family members and Selected Reserve members and their families are eligible for FEDVIP vision coverage. They must be enrolled in a Tricare health plan to be eligible. Visit benefeds.gov.

Flexible spending accounts

Flexible spending accounts can be used to defray the costs of healthcare, as well as dependent care. Troops set aside pre-tax money to reduce the amount of taxable income.

The accounts are sponsored by the Office of Personnel Management through the Federal Flexible Spending Account Program. The open season sign-up for these accounts ends Dec. 14.

For more information and to set up accounts for 2027, visit fsafeds.gov.

Officials advise troops to take advantage of the Defense Department’s free counseling and advice from personal financial management counselors at many military installations, and tax counselors available all year through DoD’s Military OneSource. FSAFEDS also offers free benefits counseling.

(B) The Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Health and Human Services are authorized to enter into agreements for carrying out this subsection.
(c) Inapplicability to Certain Employers.⁠—The provisions of this section do not apply to any employer who has fewer than 20 employees.
(f) Definitions.⁠—In this section: (1) The term “employer” includes a State or unit of local government.
(2) The term “group health plan” means a group health plan (as that term is defined in section 5000(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 without regard to section 5000(d) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986).

text:
(a) Prohibition on Financial Incentives Not to Enroll in a Group Health Plan.⁠—(1) Except as provided in this subsection, the provisions of section 1862(b)(3)(C) of the Social Security Act shall apply with respect to financial or other incentives for a TRICARE-eligible employee not to enroll (or to terminate enrollment) under a health plan which would (in the case of such enrollment) be a primary plan under sections 1079(j)(1) 1 and 1086(g) of this title in the same manner as such section 1862(b)(3)(C) applies to financial or other incentives for an individual entitled to benefits under title XVIII of the Social Security Act not to enroll (or to terminate enrollment) under a group health plan or a large group health plan which would (in the case of enrollment) be a primary plan (as defined in section 1862(b)(2)(A) of such Act).

(2) (A) The Secretary of Defense may by regulation adopt such additional exceptions to the prohibition referenced and applied under paragraph (1) as the Secretary deems appropriate and such paragraph (1) shall be implemented taking into account the adoption of such exceptions.

(B) The Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Health and Human Services are authorized to enter into agreements for carrying out this subsection. Any such agreement shall provide that any expenses incurred by the Secretary of Health and Human Services pertaining to carrying out this subsection shall be reimbursed by the Secretary of Defense.

(C) Authorities of the Inspector General of the Department of Defense shall be available for oversight and investigations of responsibilities of employers and other entities under this subsection.

(D) Information obtained under section 1095(k) of this title may be used in carrying out this subsection in the same manner as information obtained under section 1862(b)(5) of the Social Security Act may be used in carrying out section 1862(b) of such Act.

(E) Any amounts collected in carrying out paragraph (1) shall be handled in accordance with section 1079a of this title.

(b) Election of TRICARE-Eligible Employees to Participate in Group Health Plan.⁠—A TRICARE-eligible employee shall have the opportunity to elect to participate in the group health plan offered by the employer of the employee and receive primary coverage for health care services under the plan in the same manner and to the same extent as similarly situated employees of such employer who are not TRICARE-eligible employees.

(c) Inapplicability to Certain Employers.⁠—The provisions of this section do not apply to any employer who has fewer than 20 employees.

(d) Retention of Eligibility for Coverage Under TRICARE.⁠—Nothing in this section, including an election made by a TRICARE-eligible employee under subsection (b), shall be construed to affect, modify, or terminate the eligibility of a TRICARE-eligible employee or spouse of such employee for health care or dental services under this chapter in accordance with the other provisions of this chapter.

(e) Outreach.⁠—The Secretary of Defense shall, in coordination with the other administering Secretaries, conduct outreach to inform covered beneficiaries who are entitled to health care benefits under the TRICARE program of the rights and responsibilities of such beneficiaries and employers under this section.

(f) Definitions.⁠—In this section:

(1) The term “employer” includes a State or unit of local government.

(2) The term “group health plan” means a group health plan (as that term is defined in section 5000(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 without regard to section 5000(d) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986).

(3) The term “TRICARE-eligible employee” means a covered beneficiary under section 1086 of this title entitled to health care benefits under the TRICARE program.

(g) Effective Date.⁠—This section shall take effect on January 1, 2008.

title: TRICARE For Life Does Not Cover Your Spouse: They Need Their Own Part A and Part B #Shorts
description:
TRICARE says TRICARE For Life coverage doesn't extend to family members: each person qualifies with their own Medicare Part A and Part B, and anyone eligible for Part A loses TRICARE without Part B.

title: Tricare Open Season 2026: Nov. 9 to Dec. 8 Dates, Who Can Change Plans for 2027
description:
Tricare Open Season 2026 runs from Monday, Nov. 9 through Tuesday, Dec. 8, 2026, according to Tricare, the military health program’s official site.
How to change a Tricare plan before Dec. 8 Tricare lists three routes on its Open Season page.
Where to compare Tricare Prime and Tricare Select Tricare does not publish a side-by-side Prime and Select table on its Open Season page.
Tricare Open Season versus Federal Benefits Open Season The two windows open together and close on different days.
Our story on Federal Benefits Open Season 2026 has the OPM dates, premiums and start dates.
text:
Tricare Open Season 2026 runs from Monday, Nov. 9 through Tuesday, Dec. 8, 2026, according to Tricare, the military health program’s official site. Changes made in that window take effect Jan. 1, 2027. The sections below cover who can change plans, who cannot, the ways to make a change and how this window differs from Federal Benefits Open Season.

Countdown to the Tricare Open Season deadline

The clock needs JavaScript. Tricare gives dates only, with no time of day and no time zone on its Open Season page or its frequently asked questions (FAQ) page, so the first two options mark midnight at the end of Dec. 8 as a planning assumption, not a Tricare deadline. On those dates clocks are on standard time, so Eastern Time is five hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Tricare’s FAQ page says that in 2026 the season runs “from Nov. 9-Dec. 8, 2026.” Its rule is the Monday of the second full week in November through the Tuesday of the second full week in December. Counting both end days, the season is 30 days long.

Tricare also says coverage “will continue automatically for 2027” for enrollees who make no change. The page gives no time of day for the opening or the close.

Who can change plans during Tricare Open Season?

Tricare says open season applies to people who have or are eligible for Tricare Prime options, including the Tricare Prime Demo, and for Tricare Select. The Prime list on the page has more than one option, so check which one you hold on the Tricare site.

Who is outside Tricare Open Season?

Tricare says open season does not apply to active duty service members, Tricare For Life beneficiaries, or people enrolled in Tricare Reserve Select, Tricare Retired Reserve or Tricare Young Adult. The FAQ lists Tricare For Life first among those groups.

Tricare’s pages do not say whether Medicare-eligible beneficiaries as a group are in or out; only Tricare For Life is named. Anyone unsure should ask the regional contractor before Dec. 8.

How to change a Tricare plan before Dec. 8

Tricare lists three routes on its Open Season page.

Online through milConnect.

By phone to your regional contractor, through the Tricare Call Us page (the page lists no number in the material reviewed here).

By mail or fax with an enrollment form.

A step-by-step guide is on the Tricare Enroll page.

Where to compare Tricare Prime and Tricare Select

Tricare does not publish a side-by-side Prime and Select table on its Open Season page. It links three tools instead:

the Open Season Road Map PDF,

the Compare Plans Tool at tricare.mil/Plans/ComparePlans,

the Health Plan Costs page at tricare.mil/comparecosts.

The page does not mention plan-change fees, and no 2027 premium amounts appear in the pages used for this story.

Tricare Open Season versus Federal Benefits Open Season

The two windows open together and close on different days. OPM says “the 2026 Federal Benefits Open Season will run from November 9 through December 14, 2026.” Tricare describes that window as covering dental and vision plans, and OPM’s release also covers Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB). Our story on Federal Benefits Open Season 2026 has the OPM dates, premiums and start dates. Someone in both systems should note that Dec. 8 comes six days before Dec. 14.

description:
TRICARE 2027 costs are posted: retiree Prime is $396 or $480 a year, Young Adult Prime is $893 a month, and pharmacy copays stay frozen.
Which TRICARE 2027 Costs Apply to You: Group A or Group B Your costs depend on your beneficiary category and your group.
The premium plans (TRICARE Reserve Select, TRICARE Retired Reserve and TRICARE Young Adult) follow Group B cost rules for deductibles and copays, whatever the sponsor's group.
TRICARE 2027 Enrollment Fees for Retirees These are annual fees for retirees, their families, survivors and others.

text:
TRICARE 2027 costs are posted: retiree Prime is $396 or $480 a year, Young Adult Prime is $893 a month, and pharmacy copays stay frozen. Every 2027 table.

Editor, FedTools · Editor of FedTools. U.S. federal employee with 20+ years of federal experience, publishing under a pen name to keep outside writing cleanly separated from official duties. Full bio →

By the FedTools editorial team · Reviewed by Jonathan D., 20-year federal employee · Updated November 2026

Last Updated: November 7, 2026 Reading Time: 7 min

TRICARE 2027 costs are now posted on tricare.mil, two days before open season opens on November 9. Retiree enrollment fees rise about 3.7%, TRICARE Young Adult Prime jumps 12.5% to $893 a month, and pharmacy copays stay at 2026 rates. Here is every 2027 fee, deductible, cap and premium next to its 2026 figure.

Which TRICARE 2027 Costs Apply to You: Group A or Group B

Your costs depend on your beneficiary category and your group. Both are set by when the sponsor first joined.

Group A: the sponsor's initial enlistment or appointment began before January 1, 2018.

Group B: it began on or after January 1, 2018.

The premium plans (TRICARE Reserve Select, TRICARE Retired Reserve and TRICARE Young Adult) follow Group B cost rules for deductibles and copays, whatever the sponsor's group. Only their premiums are set separately.

TRICARE 2027 Enrollment Fees for Retirees

These are annual fees for retirees, their families, survivors and others.

Plan 2026 2027 Change Prime, Group A, individual $381.96 $396.00 +$14.04 (+3.7%) Prime, Group A, family $765.00 $792.96 +$27.96 (+3.7%) Select, Group A, individual $186.96 $193.92 +$6.96 (+3.7%) Select, Group A, family $375.00 $388.92 +$13.92 (+3.7%) Prime, Group B, individual $462.96 $480.00 +$17.04 (+3.7%) Prime, Group B, family $927.00 $960.00 +$33.00 (+3.6%) Select, Group B, individual $594.96 $616.92 +$21.96 (+3.7%) Select, Group B, family $1,191.00 $1,233.96 +$42.96 (+3.6%)

Sources: tricare.mil Health Plan Costs (calendar year 2027), TRICARE Newsroom 2026 cost tables. Percent change computed by FedTools from the unrounded fees.

The TRICARE page lists two exceptions:

The Prime Group A fee is waived if you are under 65 and have Medicare Part A and Part B.

Select Group A is $0 for medically retired sponsors, their families and survivors.

The Group B premium over Group A is now $84 a year for an individual on Prime and $423 a year on Select. A Group B retiree family on Select pays $845.04 more than a Group A family for the same plan.

Retiree Deductibles and Catastrophic Caps for 2027

Prime has no deductible. Select does, and the Group B deductible rises again.

Item 2026 2027 Select Group A deductible $150 individual / $300 family $150 / $300 (no change) Select Group B deductible, network $198 / $397 $205 / $411 Select Group B deductible, non-network $397 / $794 $411 / $823 Catastrophic cap, Prime Group A $3,000 $3,000 (no change) Catastrophic cap, Select Group A $4,381 $4,538 Catastrophic cap, Group B (Prime and Select) $4,635 $4,802

The catastrophic cap is the yearly limit on what a family pays out of pocket for covered services. Select Group A keeps a $3,000 cap for medically retired sponsors, their families and survivors.

Retiree Copays: The Visits You Pay For

Most network copays rise by a dollar to five dollars. The table covers the visits retirees use most.

Network visit Prime (A and B) Select Group A Select Group B Primary care $26 → $27 $38 → $40 $33 → $34 Specialty care $39 → $41 $52 → $52 $52 → $54 Urgent care $39 → $41 $38 → $40 $52 → $54 Emergency room $79 → $82 $138 → $143 $105 → $109

Prime inpatient admissions go from $198 to $205 per admission. Select Group B inpatient admissions go from $231 to $240. Preventive care stays $0 in every plan.

Active Duty Family Members: Group A Unchanged

Active duty service members pay nothing. Family members on Prime still pay $0 in enrollment fees and deductibles.

On Select, Group A family members see no change for 2027: a $50 / $100 deductible for sponsors in E-1 to E-4, $150 / $300 for E-5 and above, and a $1,000 catastrophic cap.

Group B family members on Select pay a little more:

Group B, Select 2026 2027 Deductible, E-1 to E-4 $66 individual / $132 family $68 / $137 Deductible, E-5 and above $198 / $397 $205 / $411 Catastrophic cap (Prime and Select) $1,324 $1,372

TRICARE Young Adult Premiums 2027: The Biggest Jump

The premium plans rose the most. These are monthly premiums.

Premium plan 2026 2027 Change TRICARE Young Adult-Prime $794.00 $893.00 +$99.00 (+12.5%) TRICARE Young Adult-Select $363.00 $394.00 +$31.00 (+8.5%) TRICARE Retired Reserve, member only $645.90 $707.59 +$61.69 (+9.6%) TRICARE Retired Reserve, member and family $1,548.30 $1,697.70 +$149.40 (+9.6%) TRICARE Reserve Select, member only $57.88 $60.54 +$2.66 (+4.6%) TRICARE Reserve Select, member and family $286.66 $307.48 +$20.82 (+7.3%)

Sources: tricare.mil Health Plan Costs (calendar year 2027), TRICARE Newsroom 2026 Table 5. Annual figures are the monthly premium x 12.

Over a full year, TRICARE Young Adult-Prime costs $10,716 in 2027 and Young Adult-Select costs $4,728. That gap is $5,988 a year for the same young adult.

TYA covers adult children who have aged out of regular TRICARE and are under 26. Deductibles and caps follow the sponsor's status:

Active duty or Reserve Select sponsor: Young Adult-Select deductible is $68 for E-1 to E-4 and $205 for E-5 and above, with a $1,372 cap.

Retired or Retired Reserve sponsor: Young Adult-Select deductible is $205 network and $411 non-network, with a $4,802 cap.

If your adult child is healthy and lives near network doctors, Select at $394 a month is the cheaper door. Prime makes sense mainly when the child needs regular specialty care and lives inside a Prime service area. Compare it against the child's own job-based plan, or a parent's FEHB Self and Family plan if you are also a federal employee.

TRICARE Retired Reserve covers gray-area reservists until 60. Our TRICARE Retired Reserve cost breakdown walks through the 2026 math against civilian plans; at $1,697.70 a month, family coverage now runs $20,372.40 for 2027.

What Is Not Going Up in 2027

Pharmacy copays are frozen. DHA's calendar year 2027 notice in the Federal Register (91 FR 59115, September 18, 2026) keeps 2026 rates: $16 generic, $48 brand-name and $85 non-formulary for a 30-day retail network fill, and $14, $44 and $85 for a 90-day mail-order fill.

Active duty family members in Group A also see no change in fees, deductibles or caps from 2026.

What to Do Before Open Season Closes December 8

Open season runs November 9 to December 8, 2026. It covers TRICARE Prime and TRICARE Select. Any change you make takes effect January 1, 2027.

Find your group. Check your sponsor's first enlistment or appointment date against January 1, 2018.

Add up a year. Take the 2027 enrollment fee, then add the copays for the visits you actually expect. Prime costs more up front; Select costs more per visit.

Check the Young Adult choice separately. Open season covers Prime and Select only; it does not apply to TRICARE Young Adult, Reserve Select or Retired Reserve, which follow their own purchase rules. TYA-Prime costs $5,988 more a year than TYA-Select in 2027, so compare the two at the new prices.

Read the switch rules. Our TRICARE Open Season 2027 guide covers the dates, the Prime-to-Select mechanics and what happens if you miss the window.

Compare TRICARE With FEHB

If you are a military retiree working for the federal government, you can carry TRICARE, FEHB or both. Use the free TRICARE vs FEHB Calculator to compare your 2027 TRICARE fee against an FEHB premium for your enrollment type.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is TRICARE Prime for retirees in 2027?

TRICARE Prime costs $396 a year for an individual and $792.96 for a family in Group A. In Group B it costs $480 and $960. The Group A fee is waived if you are under 65 and have Medicare Part A and Part B.

How much is TRICARE Young Adult in 2027?

TRICARE Young Adult-Prime is $893 a month in 2027, up from $794. TRICARE Young Adult-Select is $394 a month, up from $363. That is $10,716 and $4,728 a year.

Did TRICARE pharmacy copays go up for 2027?

No. The 2027 program notice froze pharmacy copays at 2026 rates: $16 generic, $48 brand-name and $85 non-formulary for a 30-day retail network fill, and $14, $44 and $85 for 90-day mail order.

When can I change my TRICARE plan for 2027?

For TRICARE Prime and TRICARE Select, during open season, November 9 to December 8, 2026. Changes take effect January 1, 2027. Outside open season you need a qualifying life event. Open season does not apply to TRICARE Young Adult, Reserve Select or Retired Reserve.

How do I know if I am in TRICARE Group A or Group B?

It depends on the sponsor's first enlistment or appointment. Before January 1, 2018 is Group A. On or after that date is Group B.

text:
Leidos Holdings, a Reston, Virginia-based defense technology and government services company, reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $4.63 billion, representing a 4% increase from the prior-year period. The company also generated $413 million in net income, secured $5.5 billion in new bookings, and increased its full-year adjusted earnings guidance as demand for defense technology, intelligence, cybersecurity, and air traffic management solutions remained strong.

Revenue increased from $4.47 billion in the third quarter of 2025, supported by higher demand for defense technology products, air traffic management solutions, and intelligence mission support.

The acquisition of ENTRUST Solutions also contributed to growth, partially offsetting declines in certain managed healthcare and federal civilian information technology programs.

Net income increased 12% year-over-year to $413 million from $369 million.

GAAP diluted earnings per share increased 16% to $3.28 from $2.82, while net income margin improved to 8.9% from 8.3%.

On a non-GAAP basis, diluted earnings per share increased 19% to $3.62 from $3.05.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $644 million, representing a 5% increase from $616 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded slightly to 13.9%.

Leidos generated $523 million in cash flow from operating activities and $476 million in free cash flow during the quarter.

The company also returned $556 million to shareholders, including $504 million in share repurchases and $52 million through its quarterly dividend program.

Its board subsequently declared a quarterly dividend of $0.45 per share, representing a 4.7% increase from the previous quarter.

One of the most significant developments was Leidos’ continued growth in government contracts.

The company reported $5.5 billion in third-quarter net bookings, representing a book-to-bill ratio of 1.2.

Total backlog reached $49.6 billion at quarter-end, including $11.1 billion in funded backlog. Total and funded backlog increased 4% and 22% year-over-year, respectively.

New awards included a $717 million contract supporting the U.S. Air Force Air Combat Command’s intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance operations.

Under the agreement, Leidos will provide intelligence mission support and advanced data integration across 35 locations worldwide.

The company also received a $672 million Transportation Security Administration contract to deploy, relocate, and manage security screening equipment at federalized U.S. airports and major domestic special events.

Another major award involved a $318 million sole-source bridge contract supporting the Defense Health Agency’s MHS GENESIS electronic health record system.

The agreement covers system maintenance, cybersecurity, performance monitoring, technology updates, and user support.

Leidos secured a $301 million U.S. Army contract to provide continuous defensive cyber operations.

The work includes deployment of the company’s UpHold Effect Agentic SOC Automation platform, which uses autonomous AI agents to support cybersecurity monitoring and response.

In space and missile defense, Leidos received a $272 million award from Sierra Space to provide infrared sensing payloads, onboard signal processing, and mission support for 18 missile-tracking satellites.

The company also won a $170 million contract to modernize flight data processing software for the United Kingdom’s National Air Traffic Services.

Additional awards included a $160 million U.S. Cyber Command support contract, a $155 million U.S. Navy contract involving sea-launched cruise missile development, and a $129 million electronic health record agreement supporting U.S. Customs and Border Protection and Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Leidos also secured separate radar-related awards of $95 million and $41 million for the U.S. Army and Marine Corps, respectively.

The company received a $27 million U.S. Special Operations Command contract for initial production of its AGM-190A Havoc Spear small cruise missile.

These awards expand Leidos’ role across national security, defense modernization, intelligence systems, cybersecurity, and government technology services.

Leidos also completed a transaction with Altaris on October 5, 2026, contributing its Security Enterprise Solutions and Industrial Automation businesses to a newly established joint venture.

Following that transaction and its third-quarter performance, Leidos updated its full-year 2026 outlook.

The company expects revenue between $18 billion and $18.2 billion, compared with its previous projection of $18.2 billion to $18.4 billion, reflecting the portfolio changes.

Its adjusted EBITDA margin outlook remains in the mid-13% range.

Leidos increased its non-GAAP diluted earnings per share forecast to between $12.50 and $12.70, compared with its previous range of $12.20 to $12.50.

The updated guidance represents the company’s third consecutive quarterly improvement to its full-year earnings outlook.

Leidos continues pursuing its NorthStar 2030 strategy, emphasizing technology differentiation, operational performance, strategic investment, and disciplined capital allocation.

The company’s financial performance and contract backlog illustrate its established role in supporting defense and government modernization programs while providing a foundation for future revenue opportunities.

KEY QUOTES

“Leidos delivered another quarter of strong financial performance, allowing us to enhance our 2026 guidance for the third consecutive quarter. Our sustained momentum reflects the strength of our focused team, united behind our NorthStar 2030 strategy and committed to delivering on our customers’ most critical missions. Looking ahead, we’ll continue to execute our strategy with confidence, invest in differentiated capabilities, and deploy capital strategically to accelerate growth and create enduring value.”
